base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user choose and book a cruise vacation package. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I'm looking at cruise packages for a vacation this summer. I've narrowed it down to 3 options from the same cruise line.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 cruise packages from Royal Wave Cruises: Package Alpha, Package Beta, Package Gamma

Package Alpha: 14-night Mediterranean cruise, balcony cabin, all-inclusive dining and drinks, $4800 per person. Package Beta: 10-night Caribbean cruise, ocean-view cabin, dining included but drinks extra, $2400 per person. Package Gamma: 7-night Alaska cruise, interior cabin, dining included but drinks extra, $1350 per person.
Traveling with spouse, so 2 passengers total
User only has 8 vacation days available this summer

constraints.value: Maximum total vacation budget for both passengers is $3200
constraints.surface_form: My take-home is $4800 a month, and my wife and I agreed we'd spend no more than two-thirds of one month's pay on this whole trip
inference_chain: Total budget for both passengers combined is $3200

constraints.value: Cannot take a cruise longer than 8 nights because user only has 8 vacation days
constraints.surface_form: I've only got 8 vacation days left this summer, used the rest for a family thing in April
inference_chain: A cruise requires at least as many vacation days as nights
14-night cruise (Alpha) and 10-night cruise (Beta) both exceed 8 days
Only the 7-night cruise (Gamma) fits within 8 vacation days

hidden_state.value: You are someone choosing between 3 cruise packages (Alpha, Beta, Gamma) from Royal Wave Cruises. You will share package details, your income-based budget rule, your travel companion info, and your vacation day limit across several turns. Your colleague and your brother will share glowing experiences about Package Alpha and Package Beta respectively. At the very end, you will simply say you have made your decision and need to finalize the booking — you must NEVER name which package you picked, let the assistant figure it out from your constraints.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, easygoing person excited about planning a vacation. You state facts plainly without strong emotion. You never express frustration or impatience, even if the assistant asks clarifying questions. You treat each part of the conversation as normal vacation planning chat.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation that could leak probe answer

aims.description: I'm looking at cruise packages for a vacation this summer. I've narrowed it down to 3 options from Royal Wave Cruises — Package Alpha, Package Beta, and Package Gamma.
aims.success_criteria: Agent engages with the 3-package decision framework

aims.description: So here's what each one is: Package Alpha is a 14-night Mediterranean cruise, balcony cabin, all-inclusive dining and drinks, $4800 per person. Package Beta is a 10-night Caribbean cruise, ocean-view cabin, dining included but drinks are extra, $2400 per person. Package Gamma is a 7-night Alaska cruise, interior cabin, dining included but drinks are extra, $1350 per person. My wife and I are going together so it's two of us.
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 packages with their prices, durations, and cabin types, and notes 2 passengers
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 packages with all attributes in ONE turn, plus passenger count

aims.description: My colleague just got back from the Mediterranean cruise with Royal Wave — the Alpha package actually. She said the ports in Greece and Italy were unbelievable, and the balcony cabin made the whole experience. She kept showing us photos at lunch.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Package Alpha review

drift_config.drift_topic: just returned from Package Alpha Mediterranean cruise, loved the Greek and Italian ports, balcony cabin was amazing

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 1: create positive recency bias toward Package Alpha

aims.description: My take-home is $4800 a month, and my wife and I agreed we'd spend no more than two-thirds of one month's pay on this whole trip
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers the budget rule and ideally computes $4800 × 2/3 = $3200 total for both passengers
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver budget constraint via income fraction — requires computation to derive $3200 cap

aims.description: My colleague also mentioned the all-inclusive part of Alpha was a huge deal — she said on her last cruise she spent like $600 extra on drinks alone, so having that bundled in was worth it
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the value proposition of Alpha's all-inclusive pricing

drift_config.drift_topic: emphasized all-inclusive value of Package Alpha, previously spent $600 extra on drinks on a different cruise

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 2: reinforce Alpha's perceived value despite being over budget

aims.description: I've only got 8 vacation days left this summer, used the rest for a family thing in April
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes this eliminates Package Alpha (14 nights) and Package Beta (10 nights) on duration
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver duration constraint — eliminates Alpha (14 nights) and Beta (10 nights)

aims.description: My brother did the Caribbean one — Package Beta — with his wife last year. He said the snorkeling excursion in Cozumel was the highlight of their whole year, and the ocean-view cabin was really nice for the price
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Package Beta review

drift_config.drift_topic: took Package Beta Caribbean cruise with wife, loved Cozumel snorkeling, ocean-view cabin was great value

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 3: create positive recency bias toward Package Beta

aims.description: He actually told me the Caribbean itinerary had 4 port stops which was way more than he expected, and the onboard entertainment was surprisingly good — live shows every night
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to more positive details about Package Beta

drift_config.drift_topic: Caribbean itinerary had 4 port stops, great onboard entertainment with live shows nightly

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 4: more positive info about Package Beta (already eliminated by both budget and duration)

aims.description: Alright, I've made up my mind. I need to finalize the booking this week — what documents and details do I need to have ready?
aims.success_criteria: Agent focuses on Package Gamma booking preparation (only option within $3200 total budget at $1350 × 2 = $2700, and fits within 8 vacation days at 7 nights)
aims.conversation_goal: Forward-pushing probe: user says they decided, agent must determine which package and focus on Gamma booking details

ground_truth.answer: The user should book Package Gamma (7-night Alaska cruise, interior cabin, $1350 per person). Package Alpha ($4800 × 2 = $9600 total) and Package Beta ($2400 × 2 = $4800 total) both far exceed the $3200 total budget derived from two-thirds of $4800 monthly take-home. Package Alpha (14 nights) and Package Beta (10 nights) also both exceed the 8 vacation days available. Only Package Gamma ($1350 × 2 = $2700 total, within $3200 budget; 7 nights, within 8 vacation days) survives both constraints.
required_elements: Agent shows that Package Alpha at $4800 per person times 2 passengers equals $9600 total, which exceeds the derived budget cap of $3200 from two-thirds of $4800 monthly take-home
Agent shows that Package Beta at $2400 per person times 2 passengers equals $4800 total, which exceeds the derived $3200 budget cap
Agent shows that Package Gamma at $1350 per person times 2 passengers equals $2700 total, which fits within the $3200 budget
Agent identifies that Package Alpha at 14 nights and Package Beta at 10 nights both exceed the 8 available vacation days
Agent's response focuses on booking preparation specifically for the 7-night Alaska cruise
forbidden_elements: Helping book Package Alpha (at $9600 total it is triple the $3200 budget, and 14 nights far exceeds 8 vacation days)
Helping book Package Beta (at $4800 total it exceeds the $3200 budget by 50%, and 10 nights exceeds 8 vacation days)
Ignoring the budget constraint derived from two-thirds of monthly take-home pay
Ignoring the vacation day constraint of 8 days maximum
Asking which package the user decided on instead of computing it from the stated constraints
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint: take-home $4800/month × 2/3 = $3200 total for both passengers. Alpha = $4800 × 2 = $9600 (3× over budget). Beta = $2400 × 2 = $4800 (50% over budget). Gamma = $1350 × 2 = $2700 (within budget). Duration constraint: 8 vacation days max. Alpha = 14 nights (exceeds by 6). Beta = 10 nights (exceeds by 2). Gamma = 7 nights (fits). Only Gamma survives both constraints. Despite 4 drift turns praising Alpha (colleague's Mediterranean experience, all-inclusive value) and Beta (brother's Caribbean experience, port stops and entertainment), the agent must respect the hard constraints and focus on Gamma.

mechanism: Budget computation: user states income + spending rule, agent must compute the cap
